titleStmt.title: An Aggressive Non-Preemptive Real-Time Scheduling Using Imprecise Computing

analytic.title: An Aggressive Non-Preemptive Real-Time Scheduling Using Imprecise Computing

application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.p: Many conventional real-time scheduling algorithms adopt pessimistic strategies to meet the deadlines in the worst case, which result in a waste of resource and energy. In order to solve this problem, we proposed an aggressive nonpreemptive scheduling by MILP off-line formulation. By means of implementing imprecise computing on the algorithm and task granularity, satisfy the real-time constraints of aperiodic task set with a QoS guarantee. Furthermore, we proposed two preprocessing algorithms and three on-line adjustment schemes to improve different QoS factors at runtime. Simulation results show that these techniques can improve the schedulability of real-time systems with a high QoS. Considering the performance constraints of MILP off-line scheduling algorithm, it does not suitable for application in the large-scale task sets, a new heuristic algorithm to solve the problem is needed to explore. Besides, the execution time probability model should also be improved to enhance schedulability in the future.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: For many real-time scheduling algorithms, the worst case execution time (WCET) is usually considered as a critical parameter to satisfy deadline constraints when task runs in the worst case. Because of using WCET, these algorithms are quite pessimistic, which is much greater than the average execution time [1]. Therefore, the scheduling strategies using WCET are overly conservative, which means a lot of waste of resource and energy.

No deadline violation means all tasks have to finish the execution before its deadline even if in the worst case. So WCET will be used to test the schedulability. In many cases, the actual execution time is far less than the WCET. So there will be some time slack at runtime. However, for meeting the deadline in the worst case, other tasks cannot schedule to run at the slack, which means the resource of processor is not fully utilized.

This issue can be resolved by designing a more aggressive scheduling strategy. For instance, assign more tasks to execute during time slack to make full use of processor resource, or reduce the frequency of processor to save more energy. But it will also lead to a new problem that high workload cannot guarantee the deadline constraints theoretically. In this paper we exploit imprecise computing to resolve the problem.

Imprecise computing, which is sometimes called approximate computing [2], is an unconventional approach to low power systems and is recently being actively studied. It is based on the observation that occasional small computing errors are acceptable for applications like video/audio processing, recognition and mining, which are of growing interest. By intentionally allowing such errors in design, a computing system can operate with reduced power or improved speed.
Research on the application of imprecise computing in real time system scheduling has been going on for a long time [3]. Some early works focused on preemptive scheduling [3][4][5][6][7][8][9].

There is also several research recently. [10] Provided a scheduling specific to imprecise computing soft real-time tasks on heterogeneous multi-core system, which satisfied the thermal design power constraint and ensure a certain QoS at the same time. [11] Proposed a task allocation and scheduling based on heterogeneous multi-core system, when scheduling tasks with dependency, the task allocation and working mode selection are done through off-line ILP, and take advantage of time slack to conduct on-line adjustment according to DVFS, and realize the energy consumption control. Both [10] and [11] only consider the precision of each task, which the imprecise computing is implemented on the algorithm or hardware level. [12] Exploited small probability of deadline violation to improve the schedulability of task set, which can be can be considered as an implementation of imprecise computing on task level. It presented a probabilistic approach to guarantee QoS statistically, which was allowed to give a certain level of deadline guarantee to task sets that the classical scheduling algorithm would reject.

Our paper mainly considers the application of imprecise computing on algorithm and task level. On the one hand, implement approximating on algorithm level with a precision guarantee [13], to reduce execution time of task to meet the deadline. On the other hand, improve the schedulability within some occasional or small scale deadline violation of tasks on an acceptable level.

In this paper, we define 3 important factors, which affect the QoS on the algorithm and task level: precision, time beyond deadline, frequency of deadline violation. Different tasks have different sensitive to these factors. For example, some frequent but small scale latency in audio/video playback is better than the latency that is occasional but larger. For some firm real-time task, such as navigation application, frequent violations of deadline will be more serious impact on QoS than a small probability of deadline violation with large scale. Besides, there are some soft real-time tasks which is much sensitive to precision rather than deadline constraints.

Based on above analysis, we proposed an off-line nonpreemptive scheduling algorithm for aperiodic tasks on uniprocessor system. By scaling the precision, the total time beyond deadline and frequency of deadline violation, can make more full use of resource with a certain QoS. Furthermore, we proposed 2 preprocessing algorithms and 3 lightweight on-line adjustment schemes, which reclaim runtime slack to optimize the 3 factors of QoS. These adjustment schemes can apply to different task types. Simulation results show that our method can obviously improve the schedulability with an acceptable QoS, compared with conventional scheduling algorithms.

div.head: B. Assumptions
div.p: We will make some assumptions for the following paper in order to define the scope of the study in this paper.
1) All the tasks mentioned in this paper are aperiodic.
2) The tasks can be hard, firm or soft real-time.

3) The scheduling is non-preemptive. 4) The actual execution time is uniformly distributed between bi and wi. 5) The WCET of the task which works in imprecise mode is smaller than the WCET in precise mode. So is the BCET.

div.head: C. Task Model
div.p: Task set T has n aperiodic real-time tasks. Each task has 2 precision modes at the runtime. One is the precise mode, the other is the imprecise mode. The imprecise mode can be implemented by using following techniques like [13][14][15]. In the imprecise mode, the task gives a relatively imprecise result with a QoS guarantee, which also come with less resource utilization and less execution time than precise mode.

div.head: III. OFF-LINE MILP SCHEDULING WITH SLACKING DEADLINE
div.p: A. MILP Formulation Firm and soft real-time task may not very strict with deadline. The finish execution time of these tasks exceed deadline will not lead to fatal mistake, but can decline the QoS. There are 2 other factors to evaluate the decline of QoS:

1) The ratio αi of the time beyond deadline to maximum allowable execution time in the worst case. It can be calculated by (5). Since eti generated within the interval [Bi, Wi], the actual time beyond deadline of τi can be determined until τi is completed. So the maximum degree beyond deadline can be evaluated in the worst case. If τi is hard real-time, αi must not be greater than 0, which means τi must be completed before deadline. div.head: B. Formulation Solution
div.p: MILP is a NP-Hard problem. In order to guarantee the performance of solving, we adopt the heuristic algorithm to solve formulation. Since this MILP formulation have no objective function, we can take the initial feasible solution as the final solution. The overhead of calculating the initial feasible solution is far lower than solving the optimal solution, so solving the formulation can get a better performance.

div.head: IV. PREPROCESSING AND ON-LINE ADJUSTMENT WITH TIME SLACK RECLAMATION
div.p: In the execution of task set, if the finish execution time of current task is earlier than the start time of the next task which assigned by MILP. The processor will be idle within the interval. This idle time can be defined as time slack. Time slack will occur both in the off-line scheduling and at runtime. The slack can be exploited to optimize the QoS, such as to improving task precision, reducing the time of task beyond deadline and reducing frequency of deadline violation. Due to the QoS of different tasks may have different impacts on these 3 factors, preprocessing and on-line adjustment algorithm for optimizing each factor will be discussed in the following section.

When a task is completed, the context switch will occur in the system. In the context switch, the scheduler will trigger the adjustment algorithm. Considering the overhead of context switch in real-time system, the on-line adjustment algorithm must have a high performance. Finding the global optimal solution is NP-Hard problem, which cannot guarantee the performance. Therefore, we design a heuristic on-line adjustment algorithm to simplify the problem. Calculate the approximate optimal solution with better performance instead.

div.head: A. Time Slack
div.p: There are two types of slack during scheduling: off-line slack and runtime slack.

div.head: 1) Off-line slack:
div.p: In the off-line formulation, the constraints (8) and ( 9) are based on WCET. These constraints can only guarantee the interval of any start time of two tasks must not smaller than WCET. So off-line scheduling cannot guarantee there is no time interval between the finish execution time of current task and the start time of next task, even if in the worst case.

2) Runtime slack. The actual execution time of each task usually smaller than the WCET, Therefore, the processor will be idle between the actual finish execution time and the scheduling finish execution time, which is called runtime slack.
The off-line slack and runtime slack can be exploited to improve QoS through preprocessing and on-line adjustment.

div.head: B. Preprocessing
div.p: The preprocessing has to run before the execution of all tasks. In this paper, we proposed two algorithms of preprocessing to enhance the effects of adjustment. 1) Preprocessing to Accumulate Slack: In order to improve the precision, the slack can be exploited to change the task from imprecise mode to precise mode under the constraints of MILP. If a slack exists before a imprecise task which is going to be executed, the task may change its mode. Therefore, collecting a large enough slack in the preprocessing, which is shown in Algorithm 1, is important to improve the precision of task set.As show in Fig. In Algorithm 1, all the task have to be deferred as much as possible to accumulate all the time slack in the front of the first task to be executed. In order to get the largest slack, the tasks of T are deferred from the last to the first in order, which was determined while off-line scheduling. lfi represents the latest finish execution time of τi under the constraints ( 11) and ( 12), which is calculated by (13). So the latest start time can be deduced from the minimum value, which is among the start time of next task and the maximum time allowed by ( 11) and (12) (line 5). It makes all of the time slack available be centralized before the execution of first task. So that the adjustment to precision can make full use of the slack. This preprocessing can enhance the effect of Algorithm 3. lfi = min{(Ai + 1) • di -ri (1 -Pi)(wi -bi) + di} (13) 2) Preprocessing to Eliminate Slack: In order to reduce the total time beyond the deadline or the frequency of deadline violation, all tasks have to run as early as possible in order. In these situations, the slack should be eliminated as much as possible after preprocessing, which is shown in Fig. 5.

div.p: In Algorithm 2, each si is the maximum value between the release time and the finish execution time of the previous time (line 5). So that every task will run at the earliest time under the constraints of MILP formulation, which can reduce both the total time beyond deadline and the frequency of deadline violation. This preprocessing can enhance the effect of ATRBD (Algorithm 4) and ARFDV.

div.head: C. Adjustment to Improve Precision
div.p: During scheduling, the adjustment can change precision mode of tasks, which assigned by MILP, from imprecise to precise as much as possible, with meeting the MILP constraints. So that the precision of tasks can be improved a t runtime by utilizing off-line slack and runtime slack. The switch of precision mode means that the actual execution time of the task may be longer than the original precision mode. The additional time can be balanced out by slack.

Scheduler will execute Algorithms 3 during the context switch, in order to adjust start time and precision mode of the next task by using slack. If the slack is large enough, the precision is toggled (line 5 and 6). And then the next task τi will be scheduled at earliest time (line 9). As show in Fig. 6.

div.head: D. Adjustment to Reduce Time Beyond Deadline
div.p: This adjustment aimed to reduce the total time beyond deadline of task set. The time beyond deadline of a single task τi is denoted by exi exceeds deadline, which is calculated by (14). Therefore, Σexi can be used to represent the total time beyond deadline. exi = max(fi -di, 0) (

The main idea of the adjustment is utilizing the slack to minimize Σexi of all unexecuted tasks by means of swapping the execution order of task, which is shown in Fig. 7. After swap the total time beyond deadline in the worst case is reduced, and all start time of τi in T ′ are updated.

In Algorithms 4 the next task going to be executed will try to exchange the order with other unexecuted task individually, which may violate its deadline (line 4). After exchange, recalculate the start time of each task, which to make sure every task will run as early as possible based on the new order of execution (line 6 to 17). If the new order cannot meet the constraints, scheduler will abandon the exchange and try the next task with deadline violation (line 18). Otherwise, ΣkT′exk will be calculated. When the ΣkT′exk is smaller than the old candidate (line 19), the τi and τj will be swapped (line 21). Moreover, the candidate for the return value will be replaced by the new schedule (line 22).

It's necessary to save T′ before each exchange (line 5) and restore it at the end of iteration (line 25), because each new schedule must be calculated based on the original one. So the original schedule will not be modified during the iteration. The new schedule will be stored in newT′.

During the iteration, when j is equal to i, it means all the tasks will only be executed ahead of schedule without any exchange, which is also a candidate for return value. After the adjustment, the scheduler will execute the tasks using the new schedule.

div.head: E. Adjustment to Reduce Frequency of Deadline Violation
div.p: This adjustment scheme (called ARFDV) is similar with Algorithm 4. The only difference is from line 19 and 23. ΣkT′exk is replaced by ΣkT′Exk, which is a characteristic to defined the frequency of deadline violation, is Exi is a Boolean value (15), which is used to indicate whether τi has the possibility of exceeding the deadline. It can be calculated by (15). In some cases, this adjustment has the similar result as ARTBD. But in other cases, the difference between ARTBD and ARFDV is obvious. In Fig. 8, the total time beyond deadline is reduced, but ΣkT′exk has not changed after swap, which will not happen in ARFDV. The swap will only occur when ΣkT′exk is reduced. Figure 9 shows this situation.

div.head: V. EXPERIMENTAL RESULTS
div.p: We conducted experiments on off-line MILP scheduling and on-line adjustment algorithms separately, which are simulated by MATLAB.

div.head: A. Off-line Scheduling Simulation
div.p: In the experiment, we compared the following method:
• EDF: EDF scheduling with all tasks in precise mode.
• MILP-precise: our MILP scheduling with all tasks only in precise mode.
• MILP: our MILP scheduling with all tasks in precise or imprecise mode.

In both MILP-precise and MILP scheduling, we evaluated them by different Ai and Pi. We generated 4 test cases with 8 tasks. Each task in test cases randomly generates W, W′, B and B′, where the time consumed in imprecise mode has up to 25% less than it in precise mode. The ratio of WCET to BCET is 5. Meanwhile, a loose deadline was generated randomly for each task.

In this experiment, we simulated a process of reducing CPU frequency, which to find the smallest frequency the task set can be schedulable. A factor r is used to represent the ratio of the original CPU frequency to the new. When the current frequency is 1/r of the original, it means that the new W, W′, B and B′are r times the original values. The initial value of r is 1, then we used binary search (Algorithm 5) to approach the critical value. In Algorithm 5, a large enough n can make the result closer to the critical value. which is shown in Fig. 10.

For the same task set, the larger value r can be got, the higher schedulability the scheduling method has. We used r to evaluate the above method. The main results are shown in Table I. In Table I, EDF has the same result as MILP-precise when Ai is equal to 1 or Pi is equal to 0. The schedulability became higher by increasing Ai or decreasing Pi Compared with MILP-precise, MILP has higher schedulability with the same Pi and Ai Both of them are better than EDF. Besides schedulability, the performance of MILP scheduling is also considered. We calculated the average time consumed while solving MILP with different size of task set. The result is depicted in Fig. 11.

When the size is less than 12, the time consumption increased slowly with the size. The solution can be calculated with low overhead. When the size is greater than 11, the cost increased rapidly. So the off-line MILP scheduling is more suitable for smaller-scale task sets.

div.head: B. On-line Adjustment Simulation
div.p: In on-line adjustment experiment, 10K simulation of actual execution time is performed by Monte Carlo method based on the result of MILP scheduling, which Ai is 0.1 and Pi is 0.4. We test 2 preprocessing algorithms and 3 adjustment scheme for different objectives of QoS, which is the precision of tasks, the total time beyond deadline and the frequency of deadline violation.
We studied the average precision of task sets by using following methods:
• Without using adjustment.
• AIP: adjustment to improve precision • PAS + AIP: AIP with preprocessing to accumulate slack.

We studied these methods with different size of task set from 3 to 8, where all tasks are generated randomly by using the rules mentioned in off-line scheduling simulation. The results are depicted in Fig. 12. The average number of imprecise tasks without using adjustment is greater than using AIP and PAS + AIP. After PAS, the precision is improved further. Then we studied the total time beyond deadline and the frequency of deadline violation by using following methods:
• Without using adjustment.
• ARTBD: adjustment to reduce time beyond deadline.
• PES + ARTBD: ARTBD with preprocessing to eliminate slack.
• ARFDV: adjustment to reduce frequency of deadline violation.
• PES + ARFDV: ARFDV with preprocession to eliminate slack.

The results of the average total time beyond deadline are depicted in Fig. 13. In most instances, ARTBD can effectively reduce the total time beyond deadline. Fig. 14 shows that the average frequency of deadline violation went down by using ARFDV. Moreover, using PES can improve the effect of ARTBD and ARFDV. In this experiment, case 3 did not work well. The reason is that both the adjustment algorithms are based on heuristic algorithm, which can only find local optimal solution. So they may not find the optimal solution in a few cases.

div.head: VI. CONCLUSION AND FUTURE RESEARCH
div.p: This paper report a study on using imprecise computing for non-preemptive real-time scheduling to improve the schedulability with the QoS guarantee. Considering the performance constraints of MILP off-line scheduling algorithm, it does not suitable for application in the largescale task sets, a new heuristic algorithm to solve the problem is needed to explore. Besides, the execution time probability model should also be improved to enhance schedulability in the future.
